source_title: Would you watch a 90-minute-long video on Instagram? - The Hindu
source_excerpt: Instagram is looking to attract viewers of long-form video content to its platform with the announcement of horizontal, up to 90-minute-long video posting options. The feature could potentially upend how social media users, content creators, and even streaming competitors operate. Amusing or addictive? The algorithms powering our social feeds storyline 1 On October 26, Instagram’s chief Adam Mosseri introduced the posting option as ‘Features,’ and showed how it works by sharing a six-minute-long horizontal video on his account. While admitting that he hadn’t always been in favour of long videos, as they could replace the time users spent interacting with others, he explained that both formats — short and long — were meant to benefit each other. In essence, users will be able to enjoy both bite-sized Reels and in-depth Features. “It’s early, and we’re testing and listening to feedback as we go. But we’re excited to give creators more room to tell their stories with the communities they’ve already built here. More to come,” posted Mr. Mosseri. Doesn’t Instagram already have long videos? While creators can record, edit and share videos that are up to 20 minutes long, Reels over three minutes aren’t recommended to new audiences. In other words, the app rewards creators who post shorter videos. While there are longer time limits for desktop video uploads, video posts, and livestreams (based on user eligibility), it’s well understood that posting long videos on Instagram is a poor way for smaller creators to promote themselves. This is a frustrating barrier for filmmakers, journalists, scholars, reviewers, and domain experts who may want to post more in-depth content, but also need engagement from new watchers. As a workaround, such creators often crop their long videos to make Instagram-friendly teasers, trailers, clips and excerpts. Using these, they invite viewers to watch their longer videos on other platforms — such as Instagram rivals YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and more. Previously, Instagram had a separate video app called IGTV, which was cut off in February 2022 to make video “as simple as possible to discover and create.” The company also said it believed that it was easier to have all videos available on the main Instagram app. Instagram’s announcement of Features appears to build on this learning: it is designed to keep video watchers firmly planted in Instagram. What does this mean for watchers, creators, and competitors? Users can look forward to longer horizontal videos even as they enjoy existing Reels. Those fatigued by a repetitive stream of overused sounds, visuals, and sped-up content may find longer videos to be a refreshing change. Furthermore, if users want to catch up with a familiar creator’s work, they may no longer need to switch to YouTube, Spotify, or another platform that better supports longer content formats. For creators, the move could mean that Instagram is not just the launchpad that sends viewers to the real home of their content. Rather, creators could consider investing in Instagram and optimising their long-form content for the platform — provided Meta gives them attractive monetisation options. (Ads in longer videos are also less likely to irritate viewers than ads within or between Reels.) “We understand the economics matter a ton, and are exploring multiple options to help long-form creators get paid,” Mr. Mosseri acknowledged on X. Despite the friction of jumping out of Instagram and into another app, YouTube is a formidable competitor for Meta. The Alphabet-owned video platform promotes its own Shorts that compete with Reels, and has beaten out even dedicated streaming giants such as Netflix, Disney, and Amazon Prime Video, when it comes to watch times in the U.S. Giving users the flexibility to create and watch both long and short-form videos on the same app could also help Instagram dent the popularity of TikTok in the U.S. As it rolls out, the true test for Instagram’s Features is whether it can break the ties between established long form content giants and the numerous creators who have built careers on them. An easy guide to Instagram’s video formats Let’s take the example of a cook-turned-influencer on Instagram who is showing off the delicious pizza they made from scratch Instagram Reels: The cook uses trending music and viral references from a well-known Hollywood film to show off the decorated pizza and introduce themselves to new viewers, in a polished video. This earns them engagement from users they don’t know. Instagram Video Posts: The cook shoots a cute video showing their toddler enjoying the pizza during their birthday party. Followers leave emojis and positive comments. Instagram Live [for eligible accounts]: The cook livestreams the moment when they remove the smoking pizza from the oven. They scream and drop the camera when they burn their hand. Those tuning in get to see all of this happening in real time. Instagram Features [under testing]: The cook can film an hour-long ‘Bake with Me’ pizza-making tutorial, so that the viewer can make a pizza along with them. Instagram Series [under testing]: The cook creates a series of linked episodes focused on buying pizza ingredients, making the crust, spicing the sauce, preparing the oven, putting the pizza together, and pairing it with drinks. Instagram Stories: The cook shoots a video of themselves sleepily shopping for pizza ingredients in their pyjamas; the video is shown to followers and will disappear in 24 hours.
